title: digitalis mariana subsp. heywoodii
intro: Digitalis mariana subsp. heywoodii, commonly known as the foxglove, is a plant species that belongs to the Apocynaceae family and is native to the Western Mediterranean region. The health benefits of Digitalis mariana subsp. heywoodii include its potential use in reducing inflammation and its cardiotonic properties, which may help in treating cardiovascular conditions. The therapeutic actions of this plant are attributed to its bioactive constituents, including glycosides, which act as cardiotonics by increasing the force of heart contractions and improving cardiac output. The bioactive constituents of Digitalis mariana subsp. heywoodii include digitoxigenin, digoxin, and digoxose, which have been reported to possess anti-inflammatory and cardiotonic properties.
